title: Zolotarev's Lemma — Milestone 1: The Cycle Producer for the Permutation-Sign Route to QR
description: Milestone 1 of the permutation-sign (Zolotarev) route to quadratic reciprocity, machine-checked in Lean 4. Supplies the producer lemma Mathlib lacks — left-multiplication by a generator of a finite group is a single cycle — and derives the Zolotarev sign computation sign(mulLeft (g^k)) = (-1)^k. The headline identity legendreSym p a = sign(mulLeft a) and Milestone 2 (reciprocity from the grid-transpose sign) are NOT yet formalized and remain open.

overview.historicalContext: Zolotarev's lemma (1872) gives a strikingly different proof of Gauss's Law of Quadratic Reciprocity using the sign of a permutation. For an odd prime p and a coprime to p, the map x ↦ a·x is a permutation π_a of the nonzero residues (ZMod p)ˣ, and Zolotarev's lemma states that the Legendre symbol equals its sign: (a/p) = sign(π_a). Reciprocity then follows by computing the sign of a single 'grid transpose' permutation in two ways. The argument is purely combinatorial — no Gauss sums or quadratic forms — and is one of the cleanest routes to the 'golden theorem'. This entry formalizes the first milestone of that route: the group-theoretic engine that turns 'multiplication by a generator' into a cycle whose sign is computable.
overview.problemStatement: Formalize the permutation-sign (Zolotarev) route to quadratic reciprocity in Lean 4. The open question asks for an algorithmic/permutation-sign proof organized around Zolotarev's lemma. Milestone 1 (this entry): supply the reusable group-theoretic core — that left-multiplication by a generator of a finite group is a single cycle, and hence that sign(mulLeft (g^k)) = (-1)^k for even-order groups. This is the producer lemma Mathlib does not provide.
overview.proofStrategy: The producer lemma isCycle_mulLeft_of_generator discharges the IsCycle constructor with base point x = 1: mulLeft g moves 1 (since g ≠ 1, forced by generation plus card ≥ 2), and every y lies on the cycle of 1 because y ∈ zpowers g gives i with g^i = y, while (mulLeft g)^i applied to 1 equals g^i. The key wiring (mulLeft g)^i = mulLeft (g^i) is obtained from map_zpow applied to the inline monoid hom a ↦ Equiv.mulLeft a : G →* Perm G — Mathlib has no mulLeft_zpow/mulLeft_pow lemma at this pin, so the hom is bundled inline. Then sign_mulLeft_generator computes the sign: the support of mulLeft g is all of G (no fixed points since g ≠ 1), so IsCycle.sign gives sign = -(-1)^card, and card even collapses (-1)^card to 1, yielding -1. Finally sign_mulLeft_eq_neg_one_zpow factors mulLeft (g^k) = (mulLeft g)^k and uses that sign is a MonoidHom (map_zpow again) to get (-1)^k.
keyInsights: The single lemma Mathlib lacks is a PRODUCER, not a consumer: Mathlib proves what a cycle's sign and order are (IsCycle.sign, IsCycle.orderOf) but not that mulLeft by a generator IS a cycle. Isolating this is the genuinely-new content.

There is no mulLeft_zpow/mulLeft_pow lemma in Mathlib at rev 2df2f01; the clean substitute is to bundle a ↦ Equiv.mulLeft a as an inline monoid hom G →* Perm G and invoke map_zpow, which both IsCycle and sign computations reuse.

Evenness of the group order is exactly what makes the sign -1: a cycle of even length is an odd permutation. For (ZMod p)ˣ the order is p − 1, even for every odd prime, so Zolotarev's sign is always -1 on a generator.

The discrete-log form sign(mulLeft (g^k)) = (-1)^k is the bridge to Euler's criterion: once legendreSym p a = (-1)^k is tied in (k = discrete log of a), Zolotarev's lemma legendreSym p a = sign(mulLeft a) follows immediately — that tie is the remaining (un-formalized) step.

Because sign is a MonoidHom, the entire family of Zolotarev signs collapses to a single nontrivial computation: only sign(mulLeft g) = -1 on the generator must be evaluated by hand, and the value (-1)^k for every other element a = g^k follows for free by functoriality (map_zpow). This is why the proof is short despite covering all of (ZMod p)ˣ — there is essentially one sign to compute, not p−1 of them.

sections.title: Zolotarev Sign of an Arbitrary Element
sections.summary: sign_mulLeft_eq_neg_one_zpow: for a = g^k with g a generator of an even-order group, sign (mulLeft a) = (-1)^k. Factors mulLeft (g^k) = (mulLeft g)^k via the inline monoid hom + map_zpow, then uses sign being a MonoidHom. This is the Zolotarev sign computation; tying it to Euler's criterion (the remaining open step) yields the full lemma.

conclusion.summary: This entry machine-checks Milestone 1 of the permutation-sign (Zolotarev) route to quadratic reciprocity: the producer lemma that left-multiplication by a generator of a finite group is a single cycle (absent from Mathlib at rev 2df2f01), the resulting sign computation sign(mulLeft g) = -1 for even-order groups, and the discrete-log form sign(mulLeft (g^k)) = (-1)^k. All three results compile with zero sorries and zero axioms.
conclusion.implications: The producer lemma isCycle_mulLeft_of_generator is a reusable Mathlib-gap-filling result: it is the engine that makes Zolotarev's permutation-sign proof of quadratic reciprocity possible, and it applies to any finite cyclic group, not just (ZMod p)ˣ. Combined with Euler's criterion it gives Zolotarev's lemma; that, plus a grid-transpose sign computation, yields a Gauss-sum-free proof of the full reciprocity law.
openQuestions: The headline Zolotarev identity legendreSym p a = sign(mulLeft a) is NOT yet formalized: it needs the Euler's-criterion tie legendreSym p a = (-1)^k and the field-mulLeft₀ / units-mulLeft sign bridge (both prose in knowledge.md, numerically certified). This is the immediate next milestone.
Milestone 2 — deriving quadratic reciprocity itself from the sign of the grid-transpose permutation on (ZMod p)ˣ × (ZMod q)ˣ — is not yet in Lean.
Can the inline G →* Perm G monoid hom and a mulLeft_zpow lemma be contributed upstream to Mathlib, closing the producer gap for all future users?
